short: The name Dalmatae comes from the name of the Roman province of Dalmatia, and the vast majority of the Dalmatian units in the Notitia Dignitatum, as well as the Equites Dalmatae, are cavalry units. In the first centuries AD, the Roman Imperial army was primarily an infantry force, and small cavalry units performed only auxiliary functions there. However, in the second half of the 3rd century the situation changed in the direction of increasing the number of cavalry units necessary for the protection of the Roman frontiers. The reason for this was the increasing number of barbarian invasions and the territorial losses of the Empire. In 259, as a response, Emperor Gallienus began to organize a joint cavalry corps of many other smaller cavalry detachments. In organizational terms, the Dalmatian cavalry consisted of vexillations - vexillationes equitum Dalmatarum, headed by a commander in the rank of dux - dux Dalmatarum. In 269 the cavalry of the Dalmatians distinguished themselves in the Balkans, destroying three thousand Heruli and Goths in battles on the plain of Pelagonia. Trebellius Pollion in his biography of Claudius II Gothicus highlighted the «extraordinary valor» equitum Dalmatarum, shown by them in battles with barbarians in Thrace in 270 AD. During the Aurelian’s conquest of the Palmyrian kingdom (272-273), the Dalmatian cavalry was the first to engage in battle with the Palmyrians and their allies on the plain near Emesa.
history: The ‘Dalmatian horsemen’ hailed from the western Balkans, roughly equivalent to the position of modern-day Croatia. Formed later in the Roman Empire as a temporary adjunct to the Legions, they became known as a ‘vexillationes’ following a reorganisation and expansion of Roman cavalry forces. In the years immediately prior the Legions had taken some heavy losses from the superior horse units of the eastern empires. This reorganisation was almost certainly an attempt to curb Roman losses and enable them to compete with the enemy's burgeoning cavalry tactics. In any case, the Dalmatae were the largest of the newly-raised vexillationes, and contributed to Claudius II victory over the Goths – a worthy record indeed!
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
